text: {winner} stands alone under the results stage lights, beside a board that has plainly made up its mind.
{loser} studies the season sheet with the calm of someone already drafting the reply.
Shelves dusted and glass gleaming, everything is exactly as promised when {winner} arrives.
Rows of engraved plates line the wall as {loserClub} waits for the final name to be read aloud.
A long, quiet moment passes between {winner} and the results board before the figures go up.
Ribbons on the lectern, silver on the sideboard and {winnerClub} ready for its close-up.
The board glows at the far end of the stage while {loser} checks the cabinet glass one last time.
An empty velvet case waits by the results desk as {managerA} and {managerB} eye the shelves.
{winner} steps into the light and the polished floor returns the favour with a very flattering reflection.
Somewhere behind the curtain {loserClub} is already working on next season's speech.
The cabinet doors stand open, the cloths are folded and {winnerClub} looks suitably at home.
A pair of white gloves rests on the lectern, waiting politely for {winner} to pick them up.
{loser} gives the results board a gracious nod, which is the most generous thing a rival can do.
Every plate on the wall has been rubbed to a shine, and the newest one is for {winnerClub}.
The spotlight finds {winner} first, and the rest of the stage settles into respectful shadow.
On the far shelf {loserClub} keeps a spot warm, just in case the table turns next year.
{managerA} and {managerB} share the stage but not the view, and the board makes it clear why.
Matching cabinets stand side by side while {managerA} and {managerB} regard them with identical expressions.
The scales in the trophy room sit perfectly level, loaded with equal silver for {clubA} and {clubB}.
Neither name on the wall is polished any brighter, and {managerA} and {managerB} have both checked.
A single cloth passes between {managerA} and {managerB}, because fairness demands the glass be shared.
Twin shelves, twin spotlights and a results board that politely declines to pick a favourite for {clubA} or {clubB}.
{managerA} looks left, {managerB} looks right and the trophy room offers no advantage either way.
The ribbon is cut cleanly in half so that {clubA} and {clubB} can each take a piece.
Under a perfectly even light, {managerA} and {managerB} read the same line of the same sheet.
Both display cases have been wiped down to the same standard, and {clubA} and {clubB} have noticed.
A handshake hangs in the air between {managerA} and {managerB}, framed by equal rows of silver.
The engraver has been sent home early, since there is no single name to carve for {clubA} or {clubB}.
The cabinet keys sit side by side on the lectern, one for {managerA} and one for {managerB}.
Level on the board and level in the room, {clubA} and {clubB} share every inch of the spotlight.
Polish that cup until you can see your face in it, then go and find an empty shelf.
I refuse to sulk in the trophy room, {winner}, because the carpet deserves better.
Neither of us lifts it today, so the room gets a fresh cloth and a shrug.
Honestly, the trophies do the talking. My job is keeping the ribbons straight.
Mind the silver, {winner}, and please do not use it as a bottle opener.
A draw gives nobody the glory, so the least we can do is split the dusting.
Engraving takes ages, so I asked the engraver to leave room for my middle name.
Next season I bring my own cloth, and the silver will know exactly who is coming.
A draw keeps the cabinet locked, and I cannot decide whether to thank or blame the key.
Forget the medals. I am in it for the squeak the cabinet door makes.
Your display is gleaming, {winner}, and I am jealous in the most respectful way possible.
The lock sticks, so each time I open the doors I make a proper performance of it.
Nobody takes the big gold cup today, which means we get to glare at it together, politely.
Silver is lovely, but the real prize is seeing my name spelled correctly for once.
I have dusted those ribbons again and again, which tells you exactly how I took the news.
A draw hands us the same view of the silver, so gloating is off the menu.
Trophies are only metal until somebody polishes them, so I keep a cloth in my pocket.
Well played, {winner}. Please tell the cabinet it can stop looking so smug.
With a draw the keys stay in both our pockets, which makes for a very polite standoff.
This room smells of polish and fresh victory, and I am delighted to be its tenant.
Those medals look far too good on someone else, so I shall plan my revenge with a feather duster.
Every proud manager needs a locked door, a warm light and a rival who asks to see inside.
We both polish until the silver shows our faces, and nobody can say who looks better.
I keep a shelf for every season, a drawer for the medals and a ribbon for the bad days.
Your name on that plate looks very grand, {winner}, so I will read it while I make tea.
A draw will not hand either of us a trophy, but it does hand us a duster and a grin.
Anyone can own a key, {loser}, but only a true champion remembers where the spare is.
My shelf has room for improvement, so I am spending the next few evenings with a saw.
No trophy moves tonight, so the room can finally sit down and so can we.
Gold in the case, silver in the drawer and a grin so wide it needs its own shelf.

head: THE CONTINENT'S CROWN
text: The continent's top prize now lives under glass, and the club has promised that the polishing cloth comes out every single morning.

head: TOP SHELF TENANT
text: The biggest trophy in the building has finally found a home, and the manager placed it on the top shelf as though it might bruise.

head: A BIGGER KEY
text: The club needed a larger key for this prize, since the continental crown would not fit through any ordinary cupboard door.

head: LATE-NIGHT LETTERING
text: The engraver worked into the small hours on the continental plate, and the manager checked every letter with a magnifying glass.

head: RIBBON PRESSED FLAT
text: The medal that matters most across the continent has a new owner, and its ribbon has been ironed with great ceremony.

head: ABOVE ALL SILVER
text: No display on the continent sits higher than this one, where the crown now rests above every other piece of silver.

head: SPOTLIGHT, PLEASE
text: Hand over the key, because the continental prize is ready for its spotlight and the glass has never looked brighter.

head: HOMEWARD BOUND SILVER
text: Carried home in careful hands, the continent's top silver has arrived and the case already looks a little small for the occasion.

head: POLISH BEFORE PHOTOS
text: The photographers are coming, so the manager has gathered every cloth in the house and started work on the big gold piece.

head: A FRESH PAGE
text: Lifting the continent's most famous prize leaves the record books needing a clean page, and they have quietly reserved one.

head: FACING THE DOOR
text: The continental crown is back home, placed facing the door so that no visitor can possibly miss it.

head: THE LOCK CLICKS
text: The top case has been locked, and its only key hangs on a ribbon around the manager's neck, which is quite the fashion statement.

head: NAME ON THE PLATE
text: A plate bearing the continent's name is being engraved this very hour, with fresh letters soon to sit beside the glass.

head: UP THE STAIRS
text: The grandest trophy in club football was carried up the stairs and set down in the best case in the house.

head: FINEST POLISH IN TOWN
text: Few silver pieces on the continent shine like this one, and the club has bought the best polish in town to keep it that way.

head: A SHELF OF ITS OWN
text: The Europa silver has been given a shelf of its own, polished to a shine, and the manager insists it will never sit in the dark.

head: VELVET AND GLASS
text: It may not be the continent's top prize, but it has a glass case, a velvet cloth and a spot near the door.

head: THE OTHER CROWN
text: The continent's other prize was lifted with the same care given to any silver in the room, and the ribbon looks finer for it.

head: CRISP ENOUGH TO CUT
text: The engraver is cutting the club's name onto a modest plate, and the letters are so crisp they could slice the glass.

head: WORTH THE RUBBING
text: Every cloth in the house has been spent on this prize, and a fresh smudge still turns up to be wiped away each evening.

head: DUST NO MORE
text: The shelf once held nothing but dust, and now a European prize stands proudly in front of the older silver.

head: A KEY TURNS
text: The key turned on the European case with a flourish, and the spare vanished into a waistcoat pocket for safekeeping.

head: A NEW LODGER
text: A new lodger has moved into the glass case, and the manager has promised it a clean window, good light and steady polishing.

head: THE LONG ROAD
text: Some prizes take a long road to the shelf, and this continental piece was earned the hard way, through every round.

head: RUBBED TO A GLEAM
text: The polish is out again, and the continental prize is being rubbed until its engraving catches the lamplight across the room.

head: LAST TOUCH OF SILVER
text: Before the case closes for the evening, a last small piece of silver goes onto the shelf where it has long been missed.

head: SIDE SHELF GLOWS
text: On the side shelf a European prize glows under the lamp, and visitors are asked to admire it without fingerprints.

head: TISSUE AND TITLE
text: The league title has been wrapped in tissue and placed in the cabinet, where its tarnish-free shine is admired each morning.

head: SHARP LETTERING
text: The league shield now carries fresh engraving, and the lettering is sharp enough to read from the far end of the shelf.

head: DEAD CENTRE
text: The league crown sits in the exact centre of the cabinet now, rubbed until the reflection is just right.

head: POLISH WATCH
text: Cloths sharpened, elbows greased, cups visibly nervous

head: KEYS INSIDE
text: The cabinet key turns, gently, at last

head: SILVER SPECIAL
text: Buffed so hard it now needs sunglasses

head: ENGRAVED DAILY
text: Every nameplate read aloud, then read again

head: MEDAL DESK
text: Ribbons pressed flat, medals hung with pride

head: SHELF SPACE
text: Measured twice, and the plan is bold

head: ARCHIVE FIND
text: Old ribbon discovered in a dusty drawer

head: BRASS NOTICE
text: Plates buffed for the grand reopening

head: KEY HOLDERS
text: Only the caretaker keeps the spare

head: TROPHY ROOM
text: Velvet cloth, steady hand, no sneezing

head: PLAQUE PRESS
text: Every plaque checked for spelling and pride

head: GLASS CASE
text: Wiped down for guests, and for nerves

head: INSIDE JOB
text: Someone polished the shelves all night

head: SHINE ALERT
text: Gold leaf catching the lamps again

head: CABINET CALL
text: Doors open, silver out, inspection begins

head: RIBBON WATCH
text: Bows straightened for the cameras, naturally

head: SILVER LINING
text: Every shelf lined, every label spelled right

head: TOP SHELF
text: Only the very best gets a step ladder

head: MEDAL RUN
text: Sorted by weight, then by mood

head: LOCKED AWAY
text: Some trophies prefer the glass to the crowd

head: ENGRAVING NOW
text: Names carved into the base tonight

head: DUSTED OFF
text: Yesterday's dust has been politely escorted out

head: SHELF LIFE
text: Medals report a very comfortable retirement

head: GLEAM WATCH
text: Every cup in the room now smirks

head: KEEPER OF KEYS
text: The keeper keeps a list, and checks it

head: NOTICE BOARD
text: Pinned to the door: handle with envy

head: CASE CLOSED
text: Silver lined up, every label facing front

head: SPARKLE INDEX
text: Brightness rated, sheen index sharply up

head: PALACE GRADE
text: Polish applied with royal patience

head: HALL OF FAME
text: Names still climbing the wall of honour
